title: Tier Exception Criteria Table, Formulary Benefit
content:
A tier exception covers a formulary drug at a lower cost-share tier. Under the Formulary Benefit, the formulary sets whether a tier exception may be requested at all, which tiers a drug may be lowered from, and the tier it is lowered to.

| Term | Exclusive | Value | Standard | Preferred Drug List | Broad | Open |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier exception may be requested | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Tiers from which a drug may be lowered | none | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 and 5 |
| Tier at which an approved tier exception covers the drug | none | tier 3 to tier 2 | tier 3 to tier 2 | tier 3 to tier 2 | tier 3 to tier 2 | tier 3 to tier 2; tier 5 to tier 4 |
| Not available for a brand whose A-rated generic is covered at tier 1 | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |

The columns are the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary, Northbridge Value Formulary, Northbridge Standard Formulary, Northbridge Preferred Drug List, Northbridge Broad Formulary and Northbridge Open Formulary.

## Criteria notes

- A specialty tier that is not listed as an eligible tier cannot be lowered. Only the Northbridge Open Formulary lists a specialty tier (tier 5) as eligible.
- On the Northbridge Exclusive Formulary no tier exception is available on any tier.

*Hypothetical illustration.* A tier 3 brand with no A-rated generic at tier 1 is a candidate for a tier exception on the Northbridge Standard Formulary, and an approval would cover it at tier 2. The same drug coded tier 5 on the Northbridge Standard Formulary would not be eligible, because tier 5 is not listed there. On the Northbridge Open Formulary a tier 5 drug is eligible and is lowered to tier 4.
